text:
maria: Heads-up: we're proposing a small-but-breaking operator API change for Dedicated pool orchestration: separate admit/execution surfaces and add a feature-flagged v2. Need migration plan and compatibility guarantees.
kevin: 👍 can you paste the minimal change?
jamal: curious why break rather than extend? are we hitting technical limits?
maria: current surface mixes admission intent and execution wiring; it's coupling autoscaler semantics to runtime lifecycle. v2 will make admit idempotent + small token object, while exec remains a separate call. simplifies warmup accounting.
olivia: sounds good but risk is integrators (control-plane, provider-operator) assuming single-call semantics. We should support a compatibility shim for N weeks.
maria: yep. proposal: roll v2 behind a feature-flag on control-plane; operator will accept both v1 and v2 payloads for 8 weeks, log deprecated warnings, and emit metrics: operator.api.v1_calls and operator.api.v2_calls. After 8 weeks, turn on strict mode in canary then flip.
kevin: plan for playback/blackbox tests? we need contract tests and a migration runbook. Also document semantics change clearly: admit no longer waits for node allocation by default. clients must use exec to observe allocation result.
jamal: contract tests: add a golden test in prow that posts v1 payloads and asserts the operator responds with legacy leases, then posts v2 and asserts separate admit token + exec path. Suggest adding a small harness snippet: 
```bash
# smoke: v2 admit -> exec
curl -XPOST $OP_ADDR/admit -d '{"tenant":"t1","slots":2,"version":"v2"}' | jq .token > t.json
curl -XPOST $OP_ADDR/exec -d '{"token":$(cat t.json)}'
```
olivia: also need observability changes: add tracing span names `operator.admit.v2` and `operator.exec.v2`. Ensure tracing tags include feature_flag and client_id.
maria: good call. migration runbook draft: 1) announce change + sample clients 2) enable feature-flag in control-plane staging 3) run contract tests + e2e 4) enable operator shim (accept both) in staging 5) mirror metrics for 2w 6) enable in prod control-plane for 10% of tenants (canary) with strict-mode off 7) check errors/latency/cost deltas -> 8) increase to 50% -> 9) flip strict-mode for the canary operator -> 10) full prod flip after 8 weeks
kevin: what about rollback? If we see API errors, we should be able to revert control-plane flag quickly and roll operator to shim mode. Decouple releases so operator ships shim earlier.
jamal: Agree. Add a k8s ConfigMap feature_flag and a startup health-check endpoint that exposes current mode so rollout scripts can assert.
olivia: Add a compatibility lint in CI that warns when code uses the old single-call pattern (we can grep for admit+await patterns).
maria: ops question: cost model changes? v2 makes admit cheaper (no long wait), exec may increase chattiness. We'll recommend batching exec in SDK with a small backoff. Document perf numbers in the RFC.
kevin: SDK change: add `orch.admit(..., prefer_sync=false)` and `orch.exec(token)` helpers and show example for languages. We'll coordinate devex.
jamal: one more: ensure RBAC scopes unchanged. If token now contains ephemeral credentials, ensure scoped TTL and KMS encryption.
maria: yes, token remains short-lived opaque string, validated by operator; documented encryption + rotation steps in runbook.
olivia: LGTM overall. I'll draft the canary checklist and add the tracing/metrics tickets.
maria: thanks — I'll post the runbook doc and link to this thread. tagging @deploy-bot for a timeline reminder.
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: Run v2 migration checklist in 3 days (staging) and 10 days (canary). :bell:
